chunk_findings.detail: The baseline inventory assertion builds `expected` from numeric `COUNTERS` files and non-split importlinter files only. It does not account for `tests/guard_baselines/unreferenced_functions.toml`, which is read later in the same test by `_kept_unreferenced()`. With that legitimate baseline file present in the repository, `present - set(PER_MODULE) - split` contains `"unreferenced_functions.toml"` while `expected` does not, so the test fails with the “read by no guard” message even though the file is read by a guard.

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `present - set(PER_MODULE) - split == expected` only compares the top-level `BASELINES.iterdir()` names against files that are not per-module counter directories and not split contract directories. It never requires an active per-module counter directory to actually exist: if `tests/guard_baselines/git_argv/` is deleted while `git_argv` is still in `PER_MODULE`, `present - set(PER_MODULE) - split == expected` still holds, and `_module_baselines("git_argv")` returns `{}` (as exercised by `test_a_counter_whose_last_module_reached_zero_has_no_directory` in the same file). The test’s own doc says it checks that a per-module counter’s directory exists while some module still has sites, but it does not.

chunk_findings.detail: The change splits guard tests into new modules (e.g. `tests/test_architecture_counters.py`, `tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py`), but pytest node IDs include the filename. A `pytest --collect-only -q` before the change reported IDs such as `tests/test_architecture_guards.py::test_import_contracts`, and after the change they are reported as `tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py::test_import_contracts`. The manifest lists no documented rename map, so this violates the intent requirement that “the collected test ids before and after must be the same set (or a documented rename map)”; any CI/golden pin selecting a pre-split ID would collect no test.

chunk_findings.detail:
The split moves these tests to `tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py` and `tests/test_architecture_counters.py`, so pytest node IDs change; for example,
`tests/test_architecture_guards.py::test_import_contracts` becomes
`tests/test_architecture_import_contracts.py::test_import_contracts`. The stated intent requires the collected test ids before and after to be the same set or to have a documented rename map; this change provides no such rename map, so any pin/golden selecting the old node ID now collects nothing and fails.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard does not read the package lists from `pyproject.toml`; it only uses `set(extras)` to compare extra names with the hard-coded keys of `_EXTRA_MODULES`, then checks only the hard-coded module names from `_EXTRA_MODULES` against `forbidden_modules`. Given a pyproject change such as `[project.optional-dependencies] rag = ["model2vec", "sqlite_vec", "new-vecdb"]`, `set(extras)` is unchanged, and `missing` still only inspects `_EXTRA_MODULES["rag"]` as `["model2vec", "sqlite_vec"]`, so it remains empty and the test passes even though `"new-vecdb"` is absent from the contract’s `forbidden_modules`. The test can therefore silently fail to enforce the architectural guard when an optional dependency is added under an existing extra.
